completion_data.completion_summary: Completed the stale-deploy-tree detection feature (Phases 3-6): finished and verified the isolated test-deploy-freshness.sh suite (7 assertions, load-bearing per a deliberate-break check), wired the non-blocking freshness warning into command-gate-in.sh with no regression across the full core test suite, demonstrated the acceptance criterion in both directions through the real gate-in path (fresh silent, stale warns with the regeneration remedy named), and documented the detection half of the pull-only regeneration pattern.

memory_candidates.content: When measuring shell-script wall-clock cost on NixOS, /usr/bin/time is typically absent. Use bash's own `date +%s%N` before/after with millisecond delta computation ((end-start)/1000000), or the `time` builtin/keyword, instead of assuming GNU time is installed.

When resuming an interrupted implementation phase, an untracked file left behind by the prior run should be inspected and evaluated against the plan's task list before deciding whether to rewrite it. In this case a fixture-driven test suite left mid-session was structurally complete and passed all assertions against the real implementation on first run; only a minor directory-convention gap (a missing info() helper) needed fixing. Treating orphaned WIP as presumptively worthless risks discarding sound completed work.

To demonstrate a preflight-cheap staleness/drift check end-to-end without touching the real repo's state, build a scratch target via mktemp -d, deploy only the extension(s) needed into it, then hand-rewrite the recorded comparison value (e.g. via jq) to an older real commit hash rather than needing a second real commit. This isolates the STALE-direction demonstration from any risk of corrupting the live repo's own tracked state.
